title: Card Relationship Levels and Which Personal Checking Charges Make Up the Relief Pool
content:
Two cases widen the charges that make up the relief pool on a Personal Checking account, read from the owner's card payments under Personal Credit Cards, from the overdraft charges standing on the account and from a premier money market balance held under Savings & Money Market Accounts.

**First case.** Where the owner has made at least 6 card payments in the last twelve months and at least 3 overdraft charges stand, the overdraft charges, the returned-item charges and the long-overdraft charges posted inside the relief window are added together.

**Second case.** Where the case above does not apply and either the owner has made at least 3 card payments in the last twelve months or the owner's premier money market balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00, the overdraft charges posted inside the relief window alone are added together.

**Otherwise.** Where neither case applies, the relief pool is not made up in either of those ways.

**Worked pools on hypothetical inputs.** Inside the relief window an account carries overdraft charges of 35.00 and 35.00, a returned-item charge of 35.00 and a long-overdraft charge of 25.00, and the largest single overdraft charge standing on it is 35.00.

| Owner's position | Relief pool |
|---|---|
| 8 card payments in the last twelve months, 4 overdraft charges standing | 130.00 |
| 8 card payments, 2 overdraft charges standing | 70.00, only the second case being reached |
| 1 card payment, premier money market balance of 9000.00 | 70.00 |
| 1 card payment, premier money market balance of 300.00 | Neither case applies |

Both cases take the charges posted inside the relief window, whether or not a refund already stands against one of them. The first case requires both of its limbs; the second is met by either limb alone. Equality satisfies each threshold, so exactly 6 card payments with exactly 3 charges standing reaches the first case.
